name: National Automobile Museum
unique: Two hundred cars from the Harrah collection, arranged in streetscapes from 1900s to the 1950s, including the 1907 Thomas Flyer that won the New York to Paris race.
buzz: The street scenes are what make it different from a parking lot of cars; the Thomas Flyer and the Cadillac V16 are the two people photograph.

name: Nevada Museum of Art
unique: A museum with a roof deck of giant letters spelling out a landscape essay, plus a strong collection on the Great Basin and the environment.
buzz: The rooftop sculpture and the view of the Sierra are the reason to go up; the galleries are small and the building is the surprise.

name: Great Reno Balloon Race
unique: A free balloon festival where 100 balloons launch at dawn from a park inside the city, with a glow show before sunrise and a teddy bear drop for children.
buzz: The 5am glow is the photograph and the dawn patrol is worth the alarm; traffic is heavy and the parking shuttle is the way in.

name: Pyramid Lake
unique: A desert lake with tufa towers and a hot spring, home to the Lahontan cutthroat trout that can reach 20 pounds, on Paiute land.
buzz: Anglers come for the trout and the tufa formations at sunrise are the photograph; the lake is tribal land and requires a permit.

name: Virginia City
unique: A silver boom town on a mountainside with a wooden main street, saloons, a opera house and the mine that produced the Comstock Lode.
buzz: The board sidewalks and the old bars are the atmosphere; it is touristy in summer and the mine tours are the serious history.

name: Virginia and Truckee Railroad
unique: A restored steam railroad that climbs from Virginia City down toward the Carson River, on the grade that carried Comstock silver to the mills.
buzz: The open car and the tunnel are the fun and the commentary explains the mining; the ride is short enough for small children.

name: Fourth Ward School Museum
unique: A four story 1876 schoolhouse with original desks and chalkboards, built for 1,000 students when Virginia City was one of the richest towns in America.
buzz: The building is the exhibit and the classrooms are intact; the top floor view of the town and the mountains is the bonus.

name: National Cowboy Poetry Gathering
customer: Poetry people, ranchers, folk music fans
unique: A week of cowboy poetry, music and storytelling in a Nevada cow town, with workshops, dances and performers who still work cattle.
buzz: People arrive from ranches across the west and the late night sessions in the bars are the real festival; book lodging months ahead.

name: California Trail Interpretive Center
customer: History families, road trippers, school groups
unique: A free center on the emigrant trail where 250,000 people crossed the desert, with wagons, diaries and a walk to the ruts still visible in the sagebrush.
buzz: The diaries are the exhibit and the trail ruts outside are the real thing; it is the best stop on Interstate 80 between Salt Lake and Reno.

name: Lamoille Canyon
unique: A glacier carved canyon in the Ruby Mountains with 12 miles of road, waterfalls and trailheads into alpine lakes, called the Switzerland of Nevada.
buzz: The drive to the road end and the hike to Lamoille Lake are the standard; the canyon is snowed in from November to June.

name: Eureka Opera House
customer: History people, music fans, road trippers
unique: A restored 1880 opera house in a silver mining town of 500 people, with painted scenery, a horseshoe balcony and a season of concerts and plays.
buzz: The room is the attraction and the acoustics are good; call ahead, it is not open every day.

name: Eureka Sentinel Museum
unique: The old Sentinel newspaper office with its press, type cases and a wall of 19th century issues still in place, in a town of brick buildings from the silver boom.
buzz: The press and the type are the reason to stop and the museum is free; the whole town is a half hour walk.

name: Stokes Castle
unique: A three story stone tower built by a silver baron as a summer home, abandoned after a few months and now standing over the Reese River valley.
buzz: The story is better than the ruin and the view down the valley is the reason to climb the short hill; it is a ten minute stop.

name: Austin Historic District
unique: A silver boom town climbing a canyon wall on the Loneliest Road, with a church, a castle and brick ruins stacked above the highway.
buzz: The drive through town is the attraction and the grid of streets is steep; it is a good leg stretch on Highway 50.

name: Buckaroo Hall of Fame
customer: Cowboy culture people, road trippers, families
unique: A small hall in the Winnemucca convention center honoring the Great Basin buckaroos, with saddles, spurs, braided rawhide and portraits of working hands.
buzz: The gear is beautiful and the stories are local; it is free and takes 30 minutes, a good stop on Interstate 80.

name: Black Rock Desert
unique: A dry lakebed so flat and empty that land speed records and a temporary city are built on it, with hot springs and a canyon at the edges.
buzz: The playa in summer is brutal and the solitude is the point; check conditions, since rain turns the surface to impassable mud.

name: Lahontan State Recreation Area
unique: A desert reservoir on the Carson River with sandy beaches, cottonwood groves and good fishing for walleye and catfish.
buzz: The beaches are the summer swim and the river inlet is the fishing spot; the water level varies a lot year to year.

name: Churchill County Museum
customer: Local history people, families, school groups
unique: A museum with a reconstructed 1900s main street, a Pony Express exhibit and a basement of mining and ranching equipment.
buzz: The street scene is the reason to bring children and the Pony Express room is the history; it is small and volunteer run.

name: Fort Churchill State Historic Park
unique: Adobe ruins of a Civil War era army post on the Carson River, built to protect the emigrant road, with a cemetery and a cottonwood campground.
buzz: The adobe walls and the river walk are the visit and the campground is green and quiet; it is a good stop between Reno and Las Vegas.

name: Dayton State Park
unique: The site of Nevada's first gold discovery, with a five stamp mill, a tunnel and tailings you can walk among on the Carson River.
buzz: The mill is the reason to stop and the town of Dayton has a old main street; it is a short visit and the park is small.

name: Hawthorne Ordnance Museum
customer: Military history people, road trippers, families
unique: A museum of artillery, bombs and ammunition from the naval depot that stored munitions here for decades, with rows of shells and a atomic cannon shell.
buzz: The scale of the collection is what people remember and the volunteers are veterans; it is free and takes an hour.

name: Walker Lake
unique: A desert lake below the Wassuk Range where the water has receded for decades and the shoreline is a study in alkali and abandoned piers.
buzz: Photographers come for the emptiness and the mountains; the lake is too salty for most fish now and the shore is stark.

name: Cathedral Gorge State Park
unique: Soft bentonite clay eroded into cathedral spires and slot canyons, with trails through the spires and a campground at the edge.
buzz: The slot canyon trail is the walk and the spires glow at sunset; the clay is slippery when wet and the park is remote.

name: Pioche Boot Hill
unique: A hillside cemetery where the graves outnumber the living town several times over, with wooden markers and the story of a silver camp that killed its men faster than it buried them.
buzz: The handwritten grave markers and the view over town are the reason to climb; the town below has a restored opera house and a mile long main street.

name: Gold Point Ghost Town
customer: Ghost town hunters, photographers, road trippers
unique: A silver camp of 30 surviving buildings kept up by a handful of residents, with a saloon and a general store you can walk into.
buzz: The caretakers live on site and will talk about the town; the road in is gravel and the nearest gas is 30 miles away.

name: Nevada State Railroad Museum
unique: A collection of Virginia and Truckee locomotives including the Inyo, a 1875 4-4-0 that pulled the first train to Carson City, with weekend rides.
buzz: The roundhouse and the restored cars are the reason to come; the ride is short but the collection is serious.

name: Kit Carson Trail
company: Carson City Convention and Visitors Bureau
unique: A walking tour of the state capital's Victorian houses and the governor's mansion, with a audio guide and a cemetery where the city's founders are buried.
buzz: The self guided map is free at the visitors center and the October ghost walk is the local tradition; most of the trail is flat.

name: Nevada State Museum
unique: A museum in the old Carson City mint building, with a working coin press, a Nevada history hall and a full skeleton of an ichthyosaur found in the state.
buzz: The mint press and the ichthyosaur are the two things people remember; the building itself is the oldest mint still standing west of the Mississippi.

name: Little A'Le'Inn
unique: A diner and motel on the Extraterrestrial Highway at the edge of Area 51, with alien murals, a gift shop and a burger named after the nearby base.
buzz: The owner tells the stories and the walls are covered in visitor tags; it is a long empty drive and the diner is the only thing for 50 miles.
